title: What is known about 1RB1LE_1RC1RF_0RD0LB_1LD0RA_0LA0LE_0RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_1RC1RF_0RD0LB_1LD0RA_0LA0LE_0RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. About half of the tape, and a rising share, is one 24-cell word, (100)^5 000 100 000 and its shifts, repeated hundreds of times; most of the rest is made of related periodic words. A few short defects separate regions in different phases. The right sweep crosses whole runs of the word's pieces (proved in Lean). How the defects move and multiply is not worked out, so nothing is known about halting (F reading a 1).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: A with 0 under the head, 1 right, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 48,128 cells have been visited and 21,941 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.193).

claims.title: Right-sweep crossings
claims.text: C> (011)^n → (110)^n C> and C> (011111)^n → (111110)^n C>, for every n.

claims.title: A periodic background
claims.text: At step 256,099,511 the tape (24,498 cells) is E>000 10 11 W^250 ... with W = 001001000001000001001001. At the left-end samples at 106, 2·106, ..., 6.4·107 steps, copies of this word (in any phase) cover 48% to 63% of the tape, a share that slowly rises. Most of the rest is made of related periodic words such as (001)^8 (000001)^4.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 24 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..9; n = 10 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when F reads a 1, and F is entered from B on a 1. The defects between phase regions are where unusual neighbourhoods occur. Without a rule for how defects are created and moved, halting cannot be ruled out. CTL (windows of 2 to 5 cells) and NGramCPS (widths 2 to 8, history, LRU) fail.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 48,128 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: One word, repeated
html: The word 100100100100100000100000 (five 100, then 000, 100, 000) and its shifts cover about half of the tape and more as the run goes on; related periodic words such as (001)^8 (000001)^4 fill most of the rest. When the right sweep passes, it shifts the pieces by one cell (C> (011)^n → (110)^n C>, proved), and the left sweep shifts them back.

sections.heading: Defects between phases
html: Between regions of different phase sit short defects such as 0 10 1111 or 101 101. Each sweep moves them. The leftmost region grows by about one copy of the word every few sweeps (15, 21, 30, 62, 125, 176 copies at steps 106, 2·106, 4·106, 1.6·107, 6.4·107, 1.28·108). In the samples the number of defects stays small, so the machine looks like a bouncer whose wall has a fixed period but irregular phase.

What halting would need. F reading a 1. F is entered from B reading a 1 (writing 1, moving right), which happens at defects. A proof of non-halting would list the defect types, prove how each passes through a sweep, and show the list stays inside a closed family.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.193).
After 109 steps the tape spans 48,128 cells (34,846 left of the start, 503 right), with a density of 1s of 0.456.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Most of the tape is one 24-cell word repeated (100100100100100000100000 and its shifts) together with related periodic words; a few defects separate regions of different phase, and the sweeps move them and lengthen the regions.
